LESSON: WRITING 7.5.1 COMPOSITION WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.5: Writing 7.5.1 Composition Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 7.5.1 Composition Writing, part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How would you ensure that you make your composition clear and interesting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the steps in the writing process

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 7.5.1 Composition Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. write a dialogue on a given topic

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 7.5.1 Composition Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the importance of the writing process in enhancing clear communication. • Discuss the steps in the writing process, Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views. • Use a digital device to search for information and ideas on the topic-wildlife, from the internet, Adjust light intensity when using the digital device for learners with visual difficulties. • Braisntorm with peers and outline the ideas to include in a dilaogue, • Write a rough draft of the dialogue on a topic based on the theme- wildlife, Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing materials or type on appropriate adapted digital devices to make their drafts. How would you ensure that you make your composition clear and interesting? 67 • Revise the dialogue by adding, rearranging, removing and replacing ideas, words, phrases and sentences, • Edit the dialogue to check for repetition, clarity, grammar, spelling and punctuation, • Evaluate each other’s dialogue, • Share the final dialogues with others by posting them on the talking walls. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use any functional part of the body or use appropriate assistive devices as they share with others.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 7.5.1 Composition Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 7.5.1 Composition Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital literacy is developed as the learner searches for information from the internet.

Values:
Unity is enhanced as the learner brainstorms about ideas for writing compositions with peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

• Effective communication is achieved as the learner connects ideas logically in writing.

• Critical thinking is enhanced as the learner evaluates his or her own and others’ compositions.

Link to other subjects:

The learner is able to relate composition writing to essay writing in Religious Studies.
